articles.author: Daniel Burke
articles.description: Pope Leo XIV had surgery on Tuesday to remove a cancerous growth in his lung, the Vatican announced.
articles.title: Pope Leo has lung cancer, the Vatican announces after surgery

articles.author: Barbara Sprunt
articles.description: Six Democratic and six Republican senators wrote a letter calling on President Trump to withdraw from his recent deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
articles.title: Bipartisan group of senators call on Trump to rescind Russian diesel deal

articles.author: Rachel Treisman
articles.description: Locals and preservationists have long opposed Trump's plan to redevelop a municipal D.C. golf course. That legal fight escalated after the government cleared hundreds of trees on short notice.
articles.title: A judge blocks the government's tree-clearing spree at a municipal D.C. golf course

articles.author: Elissa Nadworny
articles.description: In a letter, Cornell's president apologized for what happened to the student who alleges she was raped by several men at a fraternity house in 2024 and promised 'meaningful action.'
articles.title: Cornell University bans frat parties, vows to address 'disturbing' campus culture

articles.author: Joanna Kakissis
articles.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sat down for an interview with NPR at a time of renewed tensions with the White House.
articles.title: The Trump administration warns Ukraine it could cut off intel, Zelenskyy tells NPR

articles.author: Terry Gross
articles.description: Li won a Pulitzer for her memoir about the suicides of her two sons. In her new novel, Music Against the Night, she writes about two young prodigies in the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
articles.title: Writer Yiyun Li lost both of her sons. When words fell short, she turned to music

articles.author: Greg Rosalsky
articles.description: Prices can get sticky. That helps explain why recessions hurt so much — and what policymakers can do about them.
articles.title: What ice cream has to do with this year's Nobel Prize in economics

articles.author: Jennifer Ludden
articles.description: Voters in Massachusetts will decide whether to require cities and towns to allow smaller homes on smaller lots. A growing number of states are doing the same to help ease a housing shortage.
articles.title: Voters here will decide whether to force cities to build cheaper, smaller homes

articles.author: Maham Javaid
articles.description: Nearly 200 independent candidates in more than 100 congressional races are trying to prove there's an alternative to the two party system — even though the chance of winning is very low.
articles.title: Win or lose, independent candidates want to meet voters in the middle

articles.author: Krishani Dhanji
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia missing out on $45bn of revenue from resources: Greens
As Labor prepares to introduce its bill for a gas reserve, the Greens are pointing out that there are tens of billions being left on the table because the government won’t properly tax the resource.
We’re giving away billions in resource wealth while families struggle to pay the rent, put food on the table and afford basic healthcare.
Labor can find billions to prop up the fossil fuel industry, but when it comes to making corporations like Santos, Woodside and Adani pay a fair return, suddenly it’s all too hard.
The prime minister has a kink for punishing small businesses and a fetish for humiliating his treasurer. So I say this is a consistent pattern of behaviour where the prime minister constantly goes in, overrides his treasurer, humiliates him in public. I suspect it’s going to sour the relationship somewhat.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australian politics live: Albanese says ‘completely wrong’ he ‘cleaned up’ after Chalmers on credit card ban; Coalition continues to target Aly

articles.author: Jordyn Beazley
articles.description:
Public gatherings stymied by bureaucracy, Australian Democracy Network and Deakin University researchers find
Council red tape is stymieing the right to protest, a report has said, after a regional New South Wales council told a protest organiser they needed a $20m public liability insurance policy to hold a rally in a park.
A report released on Wednesday, co-authored by Australian Democracy Network (ADN) and Deakin University’s Centre for Law as Protection, raised concerns about incidents in which councils have required protest organisers to obtain insurance when rallies are held on council land. 

 It also expressed concern about the power some regional and urban councils have to issue financial penalties if public gatherings are held without a council permit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: $20m public liability insurance to rally in a park: How council red tape hinders the right to protest

articles.author: Lisa Cox Environment and climate correspondent
articles.description:
Federal court overrules decision by former environment minister for the McPhillamys goldmine development at Blayney

Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The federal court has overturned a rare protection order issued by former environment minister Tanya Plibersek under Indigenous heritage legislation, which the company said effectively blocked a controversial goldmine in the central west of New South Wales.
Regis Resources challenged the decision by the former minister to issue the order in 2024 under section 10 of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Act.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Court overturns Tanya Plibersek’s protection order which stalled controversial NSW goldmine

articles.author: Deepa Parent
articles.description:
Rights groups warn of Tehran regime’s increasing use of executions to suppress dissent, with at least 600 this year
Human rights groups have raised the alarm over the growing number of death sentences and executions in Iran, after reports that a 23-year-old woman, Najmeh Amini, has been sentenced to death for blasphemy over a social-media post.
Amini, an accounting student, is being held in Vakilabad prison in the north-east city of Mashhad. She has been sentenced to more than 12 years in prison and death in separate cases heard by a revolutionary and a criminal court.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iranian woman handed death sentence for ‘blasphemy’ in social media post

articles.author: Amy Hawkins in Kharkiv region. Photographs by Julia Kochetova
articles.description:
Faced with deadlier threats, demining groups are coming up with new ways of working using drones and AI
Crouched over on her hands and knees in a field of weeds, Olena Kabanova is digging into the ground. With a shovel and a steady hand, the 58-year-old digs out a neat square around the spot where a mine detector has sensed a suspicious object.
Four years ago, this field in eastern Ukraine was occupied by Russian soldiers. Now back under Ukrainian control, it is littered with landmines. Civilians such as Kabanova are trying to make the land usable again.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukraine is littered with landmines on a scale last seen in Vietnam. How can they be removed?

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Jury also shown 3D reconstruction of Paddington terrace outlining prosecution version of alleged murders of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies

Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon previously visited a farm where he later tried to sink the bodies of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, the prosecution has told a Sydney court.
The rural property belonged to the family of a man the police officer had met on a dating app and the two visited the farm together months before the alleged murders.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon previously visited farm where he later tried to sink bodies, court told

articles.author: Douglas Smith Indigenous affairs reporter
articles.description:
Police have charged a 31-year-old man with the alleged murder of Jayda Allen Bonner, whose body was found in a Carlton apartment on Saturday

Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Warning: This article contains images of and references to Indigenous Australians who have died
The family of a young Indigenous woman found dead in an apartment complex in Melbourne’s inner-north on Saturday say they are “absolutely crushed and shattered” by her death.
Jayda Allen Bonner, 21, was found dead on the fifth floor of an apartment block on Cardigan Street, Carlton on Saturday at about 1.45am.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Family of Indigenous woman found dead in Melbourne mourn ‘vibrant, beautiful young girl’

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Shaikh Azizur Rahman
articles.description:
Anger at electoral roll changes has boiled over, sparking a crisis for Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist government
Born into a small village in West Bengal, Shahida Fakir had always taken her vote for granted. That was, until it was suddenly taken away. She presented officials with her Indian birth certificate and family land documents from the village going back to 1962.
Both her parents had been on the electoral roll going back decades, so she showed proof of that too. But when the final revised voter list came out in April, Fakir was not on it.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ’How do you explain the deletion of 130 million names?’ Why Indian voters are on the streets

articles.author: Robert Mackey (now); Shrai Popat, Keely Aouga and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
This blog has now closed. Read the latest here

Sign up for the US Breaking News email

Ahead of her White House podium debut, Katie Zacharia reportedly monitored Donald Trump’s public schedule every day, and monitored his Truth Social, and made sure she was on-air when she assumed he might be watching, according to Politico, citing a person familiar with the matter.
That source noted that and a number of high-profile conservative anchors – including from Fox News, Newsmax and OANN – also backed Zacharia for press secretary. She is now set to the sixth person to hold the role throughout both of Trump’s terms in office.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump repeats false claim about Iran’s nuclear weapons program at Alaska rally – as it happened

articles.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
articles.description:
FSB security agency said reporter was arrested on island of Sakhalin, alleging he was collecting information about Russia’s defences
Russia has arrested a Japanese journalist on the far east island of Sakhalin and accused him of spying, in the latest sign of rising tensions between Moscow and Tokyo.
Russian foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova identified the reporter as Yuki Imai, from the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, adding that he had been accused of “conducting espionage activities on Russian territory”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russia arrests Japanese journalist on allegations of spying

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Microbiologist Aili Wang, 32, poisoned tea of colleague in Wyoming who had pending patents, prosecutors allege
A Wyoming microbiology graduate student from China has been arrested on accusations she poisoned the tea of a colleague who had pending patents and with whom she did not get along, then tried to flee the country after police questioned her.
Aili Wang, 32, was arrested 6 October at Los Angeles international airport, where prosecutors allege she sought to return to China. With her were laptops, electronic storage devices and documents now in the possession of police, who allege Wang was seen on surveillance video rummaging through the desk of the victim who specialized in technology for disease treatment – research similar to work she had done in China.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Graduate student accused of poisoning colleague and trying to flee to China arrested at LAX

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
New recruitment campaign to target adults in their 30s and 40s in bid to create 10,000 new foster care places 
Viennetta Basterfield, 67, spent two decades fostering more than 100 children in her west London home before she and her husband handed in the reins during Covid.
Her own mother had died when she was nine and she was brought up by another woman who took her in. There was no doubt in her mind that she wanted to dedicate her life to passing that gift on to others.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fostering in crisis: can flexible care models fix England’s child placement shortfall?

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
Former investor alleges BitMEX sold products in UK despite not being regulated by Financial Conduct Authority
A cryptocurrency exchange founded by the billionaire Reform UK donor Ben Delo is being sued for £20m over claims that the company mis-sold financial products in the UK.
Lewis Barber, who is a software engineer, alleges that BitMEX offered crypto derivative products to investors in the UK, despite not being regulated or approved to do so by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cryptocurrency exchange founded by Reform donor Ben Delo sued for £20m

articles.author: Anna Bawden
articles.description:
Research shows that the best linguists process unfamiliar foreign speech sounds more like non-speech sounds
If you want to get really good at French, Arabic or Hungarian, don’t start with rote learning vocabulary and grammar, focus on how they sound instead, research suggests.
A new study of how humans learn modern languages has found that the brains of the most talented linguists hear foreign terms as random noise, not words.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stop making sense: focus on sounds to help learn a language, study suggests

articles.author: Esther Addley and George Francis Lee
articles.description:
Historic eatery in capital’s theatreland given to heritage charity after changing hands only three times in 228 years
When Thomas Rule served his first oyster to diners on Maiden Lane in London’s Covent Garden, “mad” George III was on the throne of England, John Adams was US president and William Pitt the Younger had just come up with a wheeze called income tax to pay for the Napoleonic wars.
More than two centuries later, Rules, the restaurant Thomas founded in what became the capital’s theatreland, has outlasted nine British monarchs and 45 prime ministers – but has changed hands only three times. The interior of its four-storey home, stuffed with historic playbills and vintage caricatures and gilded antlers, is little changed from the 19th century, nor has the tone of its determinedly meaty menu – think rabbit rillettes, shin of veal and roast guinea fowl.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rules, London’s oldest restaurant, donated to National Trust

articles.author: Keely Aouga
articles.description:
Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was a father of 10-year-old daughter, and overcame two bouts of cancer, his family says
Police on Tuesday identified the victim of the fatal accident at Six Flags Over Georgia as 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem of Atlanta.
Kariem fell to his death after being ejected from his seat and several others were injured in an incident involving a rollercoaster at the theme park.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man who died in Six Flags rollercoaster fall in Georgia was a father and educator

articles.author: Luke Harding, and Andrew Roth in Kyiv
articles.description:
Ukrainian president’s comments on ‘particularly vile’ strikes come after US threatened to halt intelligence sharing
Ukraine received no early warning from its partners about a second night of Russian ballistic missile strikes on civilian infrastructure in Kyiv, including a critical power plant struck after dark, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday.
The Ukrainian president had earlier described an attack involving five missiles on Monday as “particularly vile”. He emphasised that receiving intelligence from Ukraine’s western allies “helps saves lives, and this is one of the most critical issues”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Allies did not warn Kyiv of Russian ballistic missile strikes, says Zelenskyy

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Prime minister reiterates UK backing after the Ukrainian president’s latest round of difficulties with Donald Trump
Andy Burnham will host Volodymyr Zelenskyy at Downing Street on Wednesday as the UK seeks to further underline its support for the Ukrainian president, in contrast to his difficulties with Donald Trump.
The UK prime minister said his message to Zelenskyy and his country would be: “We are with you for as long as it takes.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to host Zelenskyy at No 10 in show of ‘rock-solid’ support

articles.author: Dani Anguiano and Gabrielle Canon
articles.description:
Boardwalk destroyed in Long Beach and homes damaged, while Baja California in Mexico and Las Vegas also affected
Southern California coastal communities are picking up the pieces after a weekend of extreme weather brought flooding that overtook city streets and intense waves battered beachside homes.
The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel hit Mexico’s Baja California over the weekend as well as southern California and Las Vegas. While meteorologists noted that Rachel weakened into a post-tropical cyclone as it approached California, it still left a trail of destruction.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Intense waves and floods batter California waterfront homes and boardwalks

articles.author: Keely Aouga
articles.description:
Governor Ron DeSantis says death toll ‘sad’ but praises work of local officials for helping to minimize storm’s impact
Six deaths have been confirmed in Florida in the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias.
In a press conference on Tuesday, Florida governor Ron DeSantis praised the work of local officials for minimizing the impact of the storm, which made landfall late on Friday, ⁠bringing strong winds, rain, flash floods and tornado ​threats across parts of the ​US south-east, leaving hundreds of thousands ​of residents without power.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Florida officials say six people dead from Hurricane Isaias

articles.author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
articles.description:
Vatican says pontiff had lower lobe of right lung removed in ‘successful, on schedule and as planned’ operation in Rome
Pope Leo has lung cancer, the Vatican said late on Tuesday.
Leo, 71, underwent an operation and had the lower lobe of his right lung removed, with tests confirming a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin, which followed an earlier statement saying the pope’s operation had concluded “successfully, on schedule and as planned”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer as growth removed during surgery

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
‘You don’t get to take a man from his family … and just walk away from it,’ judge says as former gang leader sentenced

Tupac trial spotlights decades of US police failures in solving the case

Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the former California gang leader convicted of murder for orchestrating the 1996 fatal shooting of rapper Tupac Shakur, has been sentenced to 40 years to life in prison.
“For three years, I’ve heard you say some variation of the same thing … ‘Yeah, I was involved in this. But I’m different. I’ve moved on. I got out of Compton. I’m a grandfather now,’” Judge Carli Kierny said Tuesday as she delivered the sentence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis sentenced to 40 years to life over Tupac Shakur’s murder

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Katie Zacharia’s maiden briefing was excruciating – at least her predecessor had delivered her propaganda hot
Well, that was weird. Katie Zacharia, the new White House press secretary, made her debut on the podium on Tuesday with all the warmth, wisdom and political dexterity of an AI avatar.
Zacharia was all stilted delivery, nervous tics and lack of eye contact. With an eerie lack of emotion, she served up pro-Trump talking points, took only three questions and vanished after 14 minutes. It was like the West Wing had turned into uncanny valley.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Enter the Zachbot: Trump’s new press secretary malfunctions on podium debut

articles.author: Sirin Kale Investigations correspondent
articles.description:
More than 50 families call for investigation into how Vincent Chan was allowed to return to job after inquiry by nursery
The parents of the victims of paedophile nursery worker Vincent Chan have reacted with fury to the news that he was cleared to return to work after “significant concerns” were raised by the parent of a young girl.
As first revealed in the Guardian, Chan was reported to his employer, the nursery chain Bright Horizons, by a concerned parent in 2021.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘There was a chance to stop him’: Parents react with fury to paedophile nursery worker revelations

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Annual update from MI5 chief highlighted a complex cocktail that could have real-life consequences for Britain
MI5’s annual threat update covers so much ground it is easy to feel anxious. The terror threat has become more diverse, with far-right anti-migrant threats on the rise; while Iran has now firmly emerged alongside Russia as a country seeking to undertake violent and deadly plots in the UK.
“There is no law of physics dictating that rising state threats will be accompanied by diminishing terrorist threats,” MI5’s director general, Ken McCallum, said, although one of his core messages was that people and the country at large needed to focus on being more resilient. “In this new world, we should expect to be tested.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Far-right and Iran add to mix of terror threats UK faces – not to mention AI

articles.author: Daniel Boffey in Port Stanley, Falkland Islands
articles.description:
Exclusive: Caution urged over Javier Milei government’s ‘red notice’ requests for arrest of individuals linked to oil project
Britain has appealed to Interpol to reject Argentina’s requests for the arrest of individuals involved in a large oil project off the Falkland Islands.
With tensions over the sovereignty of the British overseas territory reaching levels not seen since the war with Argentina in 1982, UK officials have sought urgent assurances from the international organisation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK asks Interpol to reject Argentina’s ‘politically motivated’ requests for Falklands oil arrests

articles.author: Patrick Wintour
articles.description:
Civilians warned to leave target area near Sana’a before attacks as conflict between Riyadh and Houthi forces escalates
Saudi Arabia has launched a series of strikes on a strategic oil depot on the outskirts of Yemen’s capital, Sana’a, while later on Tuesday it said it had intercepted missiles launched toward Dharan, location of the headquarters of the huge national energy company Saudi Aramco.
The attacks on both sides were a fresh escalation of the conflict between Riyadh and the Iran-backed Houthi forces. Before its offensive on Tuesday, a Saudi spokesperson warned civilians to leave the target area, in an apparent attempt to strike fear into the local population before the biggest attack so far on Houthi energy infrastructure.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi Arabia strikes oil depots in Yemen and says missiles launched toward location of Saudi Aramco HQ

articles.author: Jonathan Watts
articles.description:
Hundreds of people displaced in Bangka Belitung with conditions described as worst in a decade with wildlife also badly hit
A forest fire on Indonesia’s Sumatra island fuelled by El Niño has razed nearly 300 homes, forcing hundreds of people to evacuate, an official has said, as the country battles devastating blazes and haze.
Residents first spotted the fire approaching their village in Bangka Belitung province on Saturday and tried to put it out themselves with portable water pumps, said the head of South Bangka regency, Riza Herdavid.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indonesia wildfire fuelled by El Niño razes almost 300 homes

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
The judge who helped convict Jair Bolsonaro is caught up in a crisis that could benefit his son and damage Lula

Marina Silva on Flávio Bolsonaro: He will try to finish his father’s ‘perverse project’ to destroy the Amazon

Thundering to a crowd of thousands of far-right supporters in São Paulo on 7 September, Brazil’s Independence Day, the senator Flávio Bolsonaro focused less on his opponent in the presidential election, the leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, than on someone who is not running at all.
“Whoever votes for Lula is voting for Alexandre de Moraes,” Bolsonaro shouted, referring to the shaven-headed supreme court justice once described as “Voldemort” by Elon Musk.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How a scandal engulfing Brazil’s top court could return the Bolsonaros to power

articles.author: Andrei Netto in Paris
articles.description:
Cocaine seizures in Europe are up more than fivefold in 10 years as a host of cartels take root. A four-month Guardian investigation reveals the true scale of a continent-wide shift
A four-month investigation by the Guardian has revealed that the surge in cocaine trafficking to Europe is directly linked to the expanding presence of Latin American criminal networks in Europe, where they have forged close ties with local mafia organisations.
The investigation, utilising databases, police and intelligence agencies, along with interviews with judges, prosecutors and experts from eight countries, shows that cartels and factions from Colombia, Brazil, Ecuador, Venezuela, Mexico and the US are active in at least 12 European countries. Between 2014 and 2024, there was a 471% rise in the quantity of cocaine seized and more local laboratories processing cocaine derivatives were dismantled.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Latin American organised crime ‘may operate in 16 European countries’

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
Marches in Delhi against changes to voting registration led to dragnets, internet blackouts – and questions about India’s electoral independence. Plus, the cinematographer capturing the beauty of the mundane
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Months of simmering public anger have given rise to a season of discontent in India. In its latest iteration, the demand is for the removal of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the scrapping of a controversial electoral rolls revision that has struck 130 million people off the register. Protests have erupted every day over the past week, prompting a violent crackdown on dissenters in the capital.
Over the weekend, Delhi was effectively under lockdown, transformed into a militarised landscape of barricades, road closures and paramilitary forces marching through the streets. Ahead of a protest led by the Cockroach Janta party on Saturday, authorities deployed a massive dragnet: 245 trains to Delhi were cancelled, 45 metro stations were shut, liquor shops were closed, internet services were cut off in the heart of the city and activists were put under house arrest.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shock, anger and a crackdown: why a contentious electoral revision has sparked outrage

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Security forces use helicopters to rescue dozens of people as the two storms damage infrastructure and cause flash flooding
At least five people have died after Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel pummelled Mexico’s Pacific coast, causing flooding that downed trees and electricity poles, blocked roads and inundated homes.
Simon claimed the life of a 71-year-old man who died when a wall collapsed in Chilpancingo in the southern state of Guerrero, governor Evelyn Salgado said at a press conference.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel kill five people on Mexico’s Pacific coast

articles.author: Heather Stewart in Bangkok
articles.description:
World Economic Outlook says states’ oil stocks are low and budgets are overstretched, as it upgrades UK GDP growth forecast for 2026

Threat of AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, says IMF

The global economy “could soon test the limits of resilience”, as emergency oil stocks run low and government budgets become overstretched, the International Monetary Fund has warned.
In its twice-yearly World Economic Outlook, the IMF said global growth had withstood the Middle East conflict better than feared over the past six months.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: IMF warns global economy ‘could soon test the limits of resilience’

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Energy minister says ‘fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon’ as paramilitary group again breaches stretched defences

Why are the Houthis attacking Saudi airports and how are the missiles getting through?

Saudi Arabia has been forced to suspend all flights to and from its main international airport in Riyadh until next Saturday after a further round of Houthi missile attacks caused more damage and left one person dead. Some airlines, including Gulf Air, had already said they were cancelling flights until next Saturday. More missiles were fired at Saudi Arabian cities by the Houthis on Monday, Saudi Arabian’s military spokesperson said.
The Gulf nation announced it was suspending flights from Riyadh, its second busiest airport, after Houthi missiles killed 13 people on Saturday and left more than 300 injured. Saudi state TV broadcast CCTV footage that showed passengers deluged in smoke and falling masonry as they queued at the airport terminal to board a plane just as the Houthi missile struck.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi Arabia further suspends flights after latest deadly Houthi attack on airport

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Thousands join rally to deliver petition calling for resignation of election commissioner
Delhi police have again obstructed protests in India’s capital as thousands of people returned to the streets, led by opposition leaders, to demand the resignation of the election commissioner.
After mass unrest in the capital over the weekend, when thousands were detained and harassed by police as they attempted to take part in a protest led by the gen Z Cockroach movement, on Monday the main opposition leaders led another procession through Delhi, this time to the supreme court.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian opposition figures lead march to police barricades around supreme court

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo
articles.description:
Israeli PM calls for criminal investigation into soldiers and officers interviewed in Guardian-produced documentary
The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has ordered the country’s attorney general and the head of the Shin Bet security service to reveal the identities of soldiers and officers interviewed in the investigative documentary NAZA and prosecute them for causing “harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests”.
The award-winning documentary, directed by the Oscar-winning film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza. The film is in cinemas, including in the UK and the US, and will be shown in more than 50 countries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NAZA: Netanyahu orders identification and prosecution of film’s interviewees

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
Brussels uses WTO rules to quickly impose quota, which will halve Chinese market share to 3%

Business live – latest updates

VW boss backs EU plan to bolster domestic industry

The EU is to limit the number of hybrid electric vehicles imported from China to 350,000 cars a year, the European Commission has confirmed.
Imports have been soaring in the past two years; about 800,000 battery and plug-in hybrids are likely to be sold this year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
President Zardari suspends provincial government in escalation of tensions as Khan supporters march to Islamabad
Politicians from ⁠the party of the former Pakistani ​prime minister Imran Khan have been detained after the suspension of a provincial government now under emergency rule.
Pakistan’s president declared a state of emergency and suspended the ⁠government in north-western Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, led by Khan’s ally Sohail Afridi, on Sunday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan detains hundreds of politicians from Imran Khan’s PTI party

articles.author: Jasper Jolly in Paris
articles.description:
Oliver Blume says ‘Made in Europe’ rules to counter rapid rise of lower-price Chinese brands ‘must reward real value creation’
The boss of Volkswagen has backed EU proposals to boost its domestic industry, arguing European carmakers need to be able to “compete under comparable conditions” with Chinese rivals.
Oliver Blume said “Made in Europe” rules from the EU “must reward real value creation in Europe”, speaking in Paris before the motor show this week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Volkswagen boss backs EU plan to bolster domestic European industry

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Authorities impose strict lockdown in capital to try to stop rally against removal of 130m names from electoral roll
Indian authorities have placed Delhi under a severe lockdown and detained tens of thousands of people, including the leader of the youth-led “Cockroach” movement, in an attempt to stop an anti-government protest.
Thousands of people from across India were blocked from attending the demonstration, which had been called by the “Cockroach Janata party” (CJP) to protest against an exercise that has stripped 130m names from India’s electoral roll.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Cockroach’ leader among thousands detained in Delhi protest crackdown

articles.author: Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
Recommended dose of hepatitis B vaccine will be withheld from thousands of newborns by Danish researchers
A controversial research trial that will withhold hepatitis B vaccines from some African newborns was given approval to move forward this week.
It is a central part of the vaccine vision for Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime vaccine opponent.
This article was amended on 13 October 2026. A previous version said CIDRAP first reported news that the research trial was approved by the Denmark ethics committee. Rolling Stone had actually reported the news first.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Controversial vaccine trial touted by RFK Jr gets go-ahead in Guinea-Bissau

articles.author: Julian Borger and Rachel Savage
articles.description:
Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza

The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza.
The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the international court of justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law

articles.author: Megan Davies for MetDesk
articles.description:
Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding
Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
As a result of the strong El Niño, it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season

articles.author: Saher Ahmed in Cairo
articles.description:
Matsadaash staff allege torture and forced confessions after being held on charges of working for Muslim Brotherhood
Egyptian journalists are planning a new protest in Cairo this weekend after six colleagues were charged with terrorism offences amid allegations they had been tortured in police detention.
Last week, Egyptian authorities arrested the journalists, from the independent factchecking and investigative platform Matsadaash, accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and producing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Egyptian journalists plan weekend protest over detention of six colleagues

articles.author: South West News Service
articles.description:
Free-roaming Aldabra population far exceeds human population of Seychelles after decades-long recovery programme
A survey of the world’s largest free-roaming giant tortoise population has discovered that the once endangered species is thriving.
A population of Aldabra giant tortoises lives on an island in Seychelles called Aldabra Atoll.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scientists discover 180,000 giant tortoises on one Seychelles island

articles.author: Anna Moore
articles.description:
Gavin Guffey was 17 when he was targeted by a ‘sextortionist’ on Instagram. His father Brandon has spent four years fighting for justice, and for social media companies to do more to safeguard young users
What were the last words Brandon Guffey said to his son Gavin? Four years on, he still struggles with this question. “That last exchange, it bothers me constantly,” he says. “I think I said, ‘Goodnight, buddy. I love you,’ and he said, ‘I’ll see you in the morning.’ I sincerely hope that’s what I said. The truth is, I’ll never know for certain.”
The exchange happened in 2022, on a hot July in Rock Hill, South Carolina, where, just weeks before, Guffey had won the Republican ticket to stand for the state’s House of Representatives. The election was three months away, Guffey’s head was buzzing with politics, and he’d spent that evening at a local event.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: My son killed himself after falling for an online scam. I heard it happen – and vowed to protect other children

articles.author: Robert Mackey (now); Shrai Popat, Keely Aouga and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
This blog has now closed. Read the latest here

Sign up for the US Breaking News email

Ahead of her White House podium debut, Katie Zacharia reportedly monitored Donald Trump’s public schedule every day, and monitored his Truth Social, and made sure she was on-air when she assumed he might be watching, according to Politico, citing a person familiar with the matter.
That source noted that and a number of high-profile conservative anchors – including from Fox News, Newsmax and OANN – also backed Zacharia for press secretary. She is now set to the sixth person to hold the role throughout both of Trump’s terms in office.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump repeats false claim about Iran’s nuclear weapons program at Alaska rally – as it happened

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia faced reporters for the first time on Tuesday, delivering a brief 14-minute briefing and taking questions from just three media outlets. In her opening remarks, she praised Donald Trump’s energy policies, saying he had restored US 'energy dominance', and credited his tariffs with stopping China from producing fentanyl precursor chemicals. Asked how she would balance the demanding role with family life, Zacharia said missing evenings with her children wasn't acceptable before mistakenly referring to her husband as 'my president' and correcting herself, 'excuse me, my husband'


Enter the Zachbot: Trump’s new press secretary malfunctions on podium debut

Trump says he picked ‘devoted fan’ Katie Zacharia to be next press secretary

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Katie Zacharia holds awkward debut briefing as Trump's press secretary - video

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Katie Zacharia’s maiden briefing was excruciating – at least her predecessor had delivered her propaganda hot
Well, that was weird. Katie Zacharia, the new White House press secretary, made her debut on the podium on Tuesday with all the warmth, wisdom and political dexterity of an AI avatar.
Zacharia was all stilted delivery, nervous tics and lack of eye contact. With an eerie lack of emotion, she served up pro-Trump talking points, took only three questions and vanished after 14 minutes. It was like the West Wing had turned into uncanny valley.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Enter the Zachbot: Trump’s new press secretary malfunctions on podium debut

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
District judge Ana Reyes halts tree-cutting at the East Potomac golf course until 26 October, and now requires advance notice before making course changes
US district judge Ana Reyes on Tuesday ordered a halt to tree-cutting at the East Potomac golf course until 26 October, putting a further pause on work at the historic Washington DC course that has been part of Donald Trump’s plans to remake the country’’s capital city.
Reyes issued the order one day after a tense three-hour hearing in which she harshly criticized the government for having deceived her with its actions over the holiday weekend.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Judge orders Trump administration to halt work on historic DC golf course

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington and Helena Smith in Athens
articles.description:
White House told Guilfoyle, who is alleged to have sought a bill payment from a Trump donor, to resign from post

US politics live – latest updates

Kimberly Guilfoyle is stepping down as US ambassador to Greece after weeks of reports that she sought payment from a Trump donor in exchange for access to administration officials.
The decision, announced by the White House on Tuesday morning, ends the diplomatic career of one of Donald Trump’s longest-standing political allies. It came after the US president and Marco Rubio, the secretary of state, were reported to have grown furious over the allegations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle ousted as US ambassador to Greece after alleged misconduct

articles.description:
When asked about the decision to request US ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation, Donald Trump told the press she 'was doing a good job' but that the administration 'didn't like what we were reading', referring to allegations that Guilfoyle had asked a Trump donor to pay her credit card bill. Guilfoyle, who was once engaged to Trump’s son, Donald Jr, was a longstanding political ally

Kimberly Guilfoyle steps down as US ambassador to Greece after alleged misconduct

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump speaks on Kimberly Guilfoyle resignation: 'We didn't like what we were reading' – video

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Shrai Popat ; produced by Angus Neale ; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
Democrats have described a raid on the home of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar as “deeply disturbing” and a “rogue abuse of power” by the Trump administration. The Democratic representative for Minnesota has long been a target of highly personal attacks by Donald Trump, who claims he was not involved in ordering the Justice Department raid. Omar criticised the raid as an attempt to “weaponize law enforcement” as part of a “campaign of political intimidation” against her. Lucy Hough speaks to Guardian US political reporter Shrai Popat – watch on YouTube
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I will not be silenced’: Trump critic Ilhan Omar defiant after home raided - The Latest

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
The Maga member believes the 2020 election was stolen and seemingly her new boss is saving the world from a cabal of satanic paedophiles. She’ll fit right in then
Poor Donald Trump. His (third) wife seemingly can’t bear to be near him and his (fifth) press secretary recently abandoned him to be with a baby she had only recently met.
“She decided she loved her children more than she loved Donald Trump,” the president lamented in August when Karoline Leavitt decided to step down a few months after giving birth. “I’m very upset about this. She has to go home and spend time with her children. That does happen on occasion with some people – when they love their children.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Loves Trump, lies and conspiracies: Katie Zacharia is the perfect presidential press secretary | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Stephen Starr in Trumbull county, Ohio
articles.description:
Away from the public eye, deportation planes at Youngstown-Warren and Akron-Canton airports carry hundreds of immigrants daily amid Trump’s ICE crackdown
Just after 10.30am on a recent weekday morning, a Bombardier CRJ200 Air Wisconsin aircraft landed at Youngstown-Warren regional airport.
Having made the 75-minute flight from Milwaukee, the 50-seater came to a halt and its twin engines fired down next to another Air Wisconsin plane and a larger Eastern Air Express Boeing 737, planes that flew in the evening before from Alexandria, Louisiana.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘No one’s here, no one knows’: north-east Ohio is ground zero for ICE flights

articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
articles.description:
The pioneering computer scientist on why Trump is using ‘superintelligence’ wrong, whether AI could wipe out humanity – and how our biggest challenge will be accepting we’re not the only intelligent beings
Donald Trump is a “corrupt, senile felon” whose fixation on the term superintelligence proves he knows nothing about AI, said Geoffrey Hinton, “godfather” of the technology, in a wide-ranging interview where he doubled down on recent warnings that AI models pose an existential threat to humanity and scoffed at claims the industry could regulate itself.
The pioneering computer scientist, whose work helped lay the foundations of modern AI, has since become one of the technology’s most vocal critics. His latest remarks come after a tumultuous month during which a growing list of senior AI scientists and researchers have joined Hinton in ringing the alarm about how the technology he helped create could ultimately escape human control, sparking an industry crisis, the hasty assembly of congressional meetings and a rare global consensus that something must be done.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI godfather Geoffrey Hinton: ‘We’re creating alien beings. I’m willing to be selfish and choose humans’

articles.author: Roque Planas in Tucson
articles.description:
JoAnna Mendoza draws on unique biography to connect with voters in Arizona battleground – can she flip a key swing seat?
On a recent morning, Regina Romero knocked on a yellow door above a mat emblazoned with a cat’s silhouette and the words “go away, peasants”. A young man cracked the door open and stood there silently, a toothbrush dangling from his mouth.
After giving him a moment to finish brushing his teeth, the Tucson mayor introduced herself and asked if the man had heard of JoAnna Mendoza, the Democrat running to unseat Republican congressman Juan Ciscomani. Romero handed him a pamphlet and rattled off her candidate’s virtues. The young man stood stone-faced, until she mentioned that Mendoza had served for nearly two decades as a US marine.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Duel in the desert: US marine veteran aims to win back working-class voters for Democrats

articles.author: Walker Bragman and Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
Children’s Health Defense and RFK Jr publicly dispute recent measles deaths to ‘distract’ from damage caused and question vaccines, experts say
The six-year-old girl at the children’s hospital in Lubbock, Texas, burned with fever and struggled to breathe. Doctors soon put her on a ventilator, snaking a thick tube down the child’s throat so a machine could breathe for her; they placed IVs to rehydrate her tiny body and they prescribed antibiotics for any bacterial infections that may have taken hold in the weeks she had spent at home battling measles.
But it was too late. Within a day of being ventilated, the child went into shock, her blood pressure crashed and she went into cardiac arrest. She could not be resuscitated. Her family, and the nation, mourned: she was the first child to die of measles in the US in a decade.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Anti-vaxxers target Texas measles doctors to cast doubt on deaths amid outbreak

articles.author: Ted Widmer
articles.description:
In a recent visit to Greece, the secretary of state suggested that Europe must rediscover the values of conquest and expansion
They had obviously worked hard on the backdrop – and it was magnificent. On 7 October, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, delivered a major speech in Athens, outdoors, with the Acropolis behind him. The sun was setting, bathing the ancient scene, including the Parthenon, in the light of the golden hour.
The golden hour, but yet not quite the golden age. This was not Pericles defending democracy. Instead, Rubio offered a haunting vision of the choices facing the west, arguing that the US and Europe must rediscover the values of exploration and conquest that once drove centuries of expansion, or face decline and irrelevance.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Marco Rubio is promoting troubling ideas about ‘Western civilization’ | Ted Widmer

articles.author: Nesrine Malik
articles.description:
The latest attack by Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia may prove to be more calamitous for the region than the world imagines
On Saturday, Houthi rebels launched a shocking and deadly attack on Saudi Arabia’s capital city, Riyadh. At the time of writing, the missile strike on King Khalid international airport has killed at least 13 people and left 300 injured, marking a significant turn in a regional conflagration that is only getting more intense. It was the single most deadly attack on any Gulf country since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February. In Saudi Arabia, a country that is unaccustomed to such fatalities, the death toll is bewilderingly high and likely to prompt a bloody response.
Over the past year, the Gulf has entered a new era of instability that is not temporary and cannot be reversed. This may feel like an overstatement – casualties have been relatively low, after all, compared with Gaza and Iran – but the gradual erosion of peace and security in places such as Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE has changed the region more dramatically than its leaders would like to acknowledge.
Nesrine Malik is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Gulf has entered a new era of instability. If its leaders think they can rely on old alliances, they are wrong | Nesrine Malik

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
A fuel deal with Vladimir Putin, and sanctions against the legal institution, ram home the president’s belief that might is right
On Friday, Donald Trump drove home his belief that might is right and the rule of law is an obstacle rather than an essential foundation stone of international order. First came the escalated assault on the international criminal court (ICC), sanctioning the body itself. Then he announced a deal with Russia to buy diesel.
The US has long chafed at the notion of being bound by the rule of law that it espoused publicly. That hypocrisy now appears as a lesser vice. The president has declared that “my own morality” is all that constrains him. His brazen flouting of the law, embrace of dictators and rhetorical attacks all undermine global standards.
Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on the US, Russia and the international criminal court: Trump’s assault on the rule of law intensifies | Editorial

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Austin Sarat ; produced by Angus Neale ; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
The execution of a former US army psychiatrist by firing squad is to be livestreamed after Pete Hegseth said it would be a public event. Nidal Hasan was sentenced to death after killing 13 people at a military base in Texas in 2009. There has been widespread condemnation of the decision, including from the UN which said it would ‘amount to torture’. Lucy Hough speaks to US academic and capital punishment specialist Austin Sarat, the author of Life After Death: Surviving Execution 
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Barbaric’ firing squad livestream ordered by Pete Hegseth - The Latest

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
New recruitment campaign to target adults in their 30s and 40s in bid to create 10,000 new foster care places 
Viennetta Basterfield, 67, spent two decades fostering more than 100 children in her west London home before she and her husband handed in the reins during Covid.
Her own mother had died when she was nine and she was brought up by another woman who took her in. There was no doubt in her mind that she wanted to dedicate her life to passing that gift on to others.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fostering in crisis: can flexible care models fix England’s child placement shortfall?

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
Former investor alleges BitMEX sold products in UK despite not being regulated by Financial Conduct Authority
A cryptocurrency exchange founded by the billionaire Reform UK donor Ben Delo is being sued for £20m over claims that the company mis-sold financial products in the UK.
Lewis Barber, who is a software engineer, alleges that BitMEX offered crypto derivative products to investors in the UK, despite not being regulated or approved to do so by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cryptocurrency exchange founded by Reform donor Ben Delo sued for £20m

articles.author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
articles.description:
Body representing some of Britain’s biggest graduate employers reveals misconduct is at a record high
It is obvious when someone is using AI to drum up answers in a job interview, according to Chris Morrow, who runs a recruitment agency in Manchester.
“It’s like they are reading off an Autocue,” he said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Use of AI in job interviews on the rise – but UK recruiters say they can spot the cheats

articles.author: Anna Bawden
articles.description:
Research shows that the best linguists process unfamiliar foreign speech sounds more like non-speech sounds
If you want to get really good at French, Arabic or Hungarian, don’t start with rote learning vocabulary and grammar, focus on how they sound instead, research suggests.
A new study of how humans learn modern languages has found that the brains of the most talented linguists hear foreign terms as random noise, not words.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stop making sense: focus on sounds to help learn a language, study suggests

articles.author: Esther Addley and George Francis Lee
articles.description:
Historic eatery in capital’s theatreland given to heritage charity after changing hands only three times in 228 years
When Thomas Rule served his first oyster to diners on Maiden Lane in London’s Covent Garden, “mad” George III was on the throne of England, John Adams was US president and William Pitt the Younger had just come up with a wheeze called income tax to pay for the Napoleonic wars.
More than two centuries later, Rules, the restaurant Thomas founded in what became the capital’s theatreland, has outlasted nine British monarchs and 45 prime ministers – but has changed hands only three times. The interior of its four-storey home, stuffed with historic playbills and vintage caricatures and gilded antlers, is little changed from the 19th century, nor has the tone of its determinedly meaty menu – think rabbit rillettes, shin of veal and roast guinea fowl.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rules, London’s oldest restaurant, donated to National Trust

articles.author: Robyn Vinter North of England correspondent and Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
William Chapman was pronounced dead at scene on Saturday after scaling fence and entering enclosure 
A man killed by a tiger at a zoo in South Yorkshire has been named locally as William Chapman.
Chapman scaled the fence and entered the enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster on Saturday afternoon. Witnesses described seeing Chapman, who has not been officially named by police, walking up to a 200kg male Siberian tiger named Altai, which attacked him.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man killed by tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park named

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Prime minister reiterates UK backing after the Ukrainian president’s latest round of difficulties with Donald Trump
Andy Burnham will host Volodymyr Zelenskyy at Downing Street on Wednesday as the UK seeks to further underline its support for the Ukrainian president, in contrast to his difficulties with Donald Trump.
The UK prime minister said his message to Zelenskyy and his country would be: “We are with you for as long as it takes.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to host Zelenskyy at No 10 in show of ‘rock-solid’ support

articles.author: Sirin Kale Investigations correspondent
articles.description:
More than 50 families call for investigation into how Vincent Chan was allowed to return to job after inquiry by nursery
The parents of the victims of paedophile nursery worker Vincent Chan have reacted with fury to the news that he was cleared to return to work after “significant concerns” were raised by the parent of a young girl.
As first revealed in the Guardian, Chan was reported to his employer, the nursery chain Bright Horizons, by a concerned parent in 2021.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘There was a chance to stop him’: Parents react with fury to paedophile nursery worker revelations

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Annual update from MI5 chief highlighted a complex cocktail that could have real-life consequences for Britain
MI5’s annual threat update covers so much ground it is easy to feel anxious. The terror threat has become more diverse, with far-right anti-migrant threats on the rise; while Iran has now firmly emerged alongside Russia as a country seeking to undertake violent and deadly plots in the UK.
“There is no law of physics dictating that rising state threats will be accompanied by diminishing terrorist threats,” MI5’s director general, Ken McCallum, said, although one of his core messages was that people and the country at large needed to focus on being more resilient. “In this new world, we should expect to be tested.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Far-right and Iran add to mix of terror threats UK faces – not to mention AI

articles.author: Sarah Butler and Richard Partington
articles.description:
Retailers call on John Healey to reduce national insurance contributions threshold in his first budget
Some of the UK’s biggest retailers and hospitality businesses, including Tesco, Costa Coffee and the Co-op, have met John Healey to urge him to cut the cost of employing young people in his first budget.
At the No 11 event on Tuesday morning, the chancellor heard from sector leaders – including the boss of Marks & Spencer, Stuart Machin, and Sainsbury’s chief executive, Simon Roberts – about the impact of the rise in employers’ national insurance contributions (Nics).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK high street bosses urge chancellor to cut cost of employing young people

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
He argued there was no evidence to suggest the result of the Brexit vote had been swayed as a result of the effort

Andy Burnham promises ‘serious dialogue’ over UK’s relationship with EU

Zia Yusuf, Reform UK’s home affairs spokesperson, has said he does not agree with his colleague Suella Braverman’s assertion that black people cannot be English.
Asked about her views in an interview on Sky News, Yusuf said:
In my view Ashley Cole is the best English fullback in history, and I won’t take any other position. So in my view, Ashley Cole is English. I think the argument that he’s not English doesn’t hold water with me.
Nasser Hussain, who I grew up watching when I went to the cricket, the idea that those people aren’t English is an alien concept to me.
I would respectfully disagree with people, who make the opposite argument.
To say I’m English is to take a ‘laissez-faire, anything-goes’ attitude to ethnicity, citizenship and identity. It also denies me my Asian heritage. The liberals (many of them in today’s Conservative party) take this cosmopolitan approach to Englishness. They’re terrified of being called racist so they say that anyone, as long as they’re born here, can be English.
I take the conservative approach. Englishness is an ethnicity. There have been English people for centuries and we need to recognise this more if we are to start taking a more muscular approach to citizenship and nationality. And no, it’s not racist to say this.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MI5 chief Ken McCallum confirms Russia did interfere in Brexit referendum but says it had little impact – as it happened

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
Abta advice comes as more than more than 150 websites offer service of securing entry to Schengen zone
Britons travelling to EU countries have been told not to apply for an Etias visa waiver, with more than 150 websites touting the service despite its introduction being delayed.
Non-EU citizens, including UK travellers and those from other visa-exempt countries including the US, Australia and Canada, will soon need to pay €20 (£17) for an electronic waiver to enter the Schengen zone under the European travel information and authorisation system (Etias).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Britons travelling to EU countries told not to apply for delayed Etias visa waiver

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Ken McCallum says Kremlin attempted to influence vote through social media and TV reports but had little impact
Russia did try to interfere in the Brexit referendum through social media and television reports, the head of MI5 said on Tuesday, but he added that did not mean the Kremlin had any impact on the result.
Ken McCallum endorsed comments by Andy Burnham, who raised the issue over the past two days, though he said continuing to debate it risked giving the Kremlin a needless propaganda victory.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russia did try to interfere in Brexit referendum, head of MI5 confirms

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Nearly half of species are in decline, with farmland birds and seabirds the worst hit, conservation bodies say
Wild bird populations in the UK have fallen to their lowest level since records began, figures show, with nearly half of species in decline.
Figures produced by leading nature conservation bodies for the government show that average populations across 132 native breeding species fell by 19% between 1970 and 2025, with farmland birds and seabirds the worst hit in recent years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Shocking and sobering’: UK bird populations fall to lowest level on record

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Farage’s intervention comes as Reform chair Zia Yusuf criticises ‘everybody’ in former Tory government that included Jenrick and Suella Braverman
Nigel Farage has denied that a Reform UK government would authorise lethal force against small boat crossings in the Channel, hours after one of his MPs said the Royal Marines should be permitted to fire on the boats.
Farage overruled Robert Jenrick, a Reform UK MP who defected from the Conservatives, who had told TalkTV that the party would deploy the marines to take boats back to France.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Farage denies Reform would let troops shoot small boats after Jenrick’s ‘lethal force’ claim

articles.author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Conference to explore legacy of Naseem Khan’s seminal 1976 report about  exclusion of minority ethnic artists
It is 50 years since cultural historian Naseem Khan’s challenge to the British arts establishment was first published, and the question of who and what counts as British continues to be contested.
The Arts Britain Ignores – Khan’s groundbreaking 1976 report, commissioned by organisations including the then Arts Council of Great Britain, presented a vision of a pluralistic national culture, in which the creativity of Britons of diverse ethnic backgrounds – from bhangra music, to black painters and Ukrainian dance – should be recognised, supported and respected.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: 50 years on from Arts Britain Ignores: how much has changed for black and Asian artists?

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
Spain remains most popular destination as Britons book later in hope of better deals, Abta report finds
The UK’s cost of living squeeze means fewer people plan to ringfence money for holidays abroad next year, the travel industry has warned.
Despite war, wildfires and EES border checks, the numbers of Britons taking holidays climbed back to pre-pandemic levels this year – but rising costs may mean the numbers have peaked, according to an annual travel industry report on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fewer Britons plan to ringfence money for holidays abroad next year, says travel industry

articles.author: Heather Stewart in Bangkok and Kalyeena Makortoff in London
articles.description:
High valuations and debt put sector in danger, while fund also warns on government borrowing and cyber-attacks

IMF warns global economy ‘could soon test the limits of resilience’

The threat of an AI share price crash rippling out across global markets is putting world financial stability at risk, the International Monetary fund has warned.
In its twice-yearly Global Financial Stability Report, the IMF highlighted the sky-high valuations for AI companies along with their increasing debt pile as one reason that risks in the system are “elevated”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Threat of AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, says IMF

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Cyber-attack on TFG London comes less than a week after online fashion seller Asos was hit by hackers
The owner of Phase Eight, Hobbs and Whistles has said its websites and IT systems have been hit by a cyber-attack that may have compromised customers’ personal data.
The South-African listed TFG London said it identified the “cybersecurity incident” at the three UK-based retail chains on Sunday. Its two other UK brands, Inside Story and White Stuff, are not affected.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hobbs and Whistles owner investigates hack that may have exposed customer data

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor and Dan Milmo
articles.description:
Move from anti-immigration or anti-Muslim views to violence is ‘most marked trend’ in spy agency’s caseload over last year
Extremists with anti-migrant opinions are becoming increasingly likely to consider carrying out terrorist attacks against immigration centres and asylum hotels in the UK, the head of MI5 has warned.
Ken McCallum said a shift from radicalised rightwing sentiment to violence was “the most marked trend” in the spy agency’s caseload over the past year, contributing to a rise in the overall UK terror threat level.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rightwing extremists increasingly likely to consider terrorist attacks, MI5 chief says

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Audiences in Manchester will be asked to wear smart glasses for An Ark, which debuted in New York this year
Ian McKellen will star in a groundbreaking new play that gets its UK premiere in Manchester next spring. But the veteran actor will not set foot on stage.
The Lord of the Rings star is taking part in An Ark, a “mixed reality” play that had its debut in New York earlier this year. Theatregoers are asked to wear smart glasses, which project the actors into the room.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ian McKellen to star in UK premiere of ‘mixed reality’ play – but not in person

articles.author: Heather Stewart in Bangkok
articles.description:
Fund upgrades UK’s GDP growth forecast for 2026 to 1.3%, but says it is likely to edge down next year

IMF warns global economy ‘could soon test the limits of resilience’

John Healey should “stay the course” and continue repairing the UK’s public finances, the International Monetary Fund’s top economist has said, after the fund lifted its growth forecast for Britain.
Little more than a fortnight before Healey’s first budget, Silvana Tenreyro, the IMF’s economic counsellor, said the UK “stands out” among G7 countries in having a plan to narrow its deficit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: IMF raises UK growth forecast as economist says Healey should ‘stay the course’

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Exclusive: Homes demolished along east coast after being deemed too vulnerable to live in, figures reveal
Seaside communities along the east coast of England have lost at least 183 homes to coastal erosion and landslides over the past 16 years, figures obtained by the Guardian reveal.
After councils judged properties across the Yorkshire and East Anglian coasts too vulnerable to remain safely occupied, the homes were proactively demolished.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Coastal erosion in England has claimed at least 183 homes in past 16 years

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
Cambridge University study suggests stark gender divide in misdiagnosis, with women also waiting longer for treatment
Women with autoimmune conditions are up to 74% more likely than men to be told their symptoms are psychological or psychosomatic, and face much longer waits for a diagnosis and treatment, a study suggests.
Hundreds of millions of people – about one in 10 globally – are affected by autoimmune conditions, which can cause a range of health issues including fatigue, muscle pain and rashes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Women ‘more likely to be told autoimmune conditions are psychological’

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Over 10m people have tuned in for episodes of new season of BBC hit as mass TV audiences become increasingly rare
For the celebrities chosen as traitors in the BBC’s juggernaut reality show, the task is simple – kill off fellow contestants without getting caught.
Yet with the new series of Celebrity Traitors once again attracting huge audiences, its UK producers are delighting in one of the show’s more wholesome qualities – its popularity is staving off the death of television’s ability to unite the nation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Universal appeal’: Celebrity Traitors producer reveals secrets to its success

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Plans for a new theatre for world’s longest-running soap in Digbeth scrapped as part of cost-cutting measures
The BBC is set to stop recording The Archers in Birmingham for the first time in the show’s 75-year history, after scrapping plans for a radio drama theatre that was to be the new home of the world’s longest-running soap opera.
A pledge to move recordings to the so-called Tea Factory, the BBC’s new Birmingham hub in Digbeth, has become the latest victim of the corporation’s £500m cuts plan.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: BBC to stop recording The Archers in Birmingham for first time in its 75-year history

articles.author: Dalya Alberge
articles.description:
Exclusive: Finds suggest account in medieval folklore of a camp near Frenni Fawr hill was rooted in reality
Magnus Maximus, the Roman emperor who ruled Britain in the fourth century, led his troops against the Picts and Scots, but a theory that he also established a military camp near Frenni Fawr hill in Wales has so far been based on folklore.
Now fourth-century coins, among other finds at a newly identified Roman fort in Pembrokeshire, suggest the medieval tale was rooted in reality, to the excitement of archaeologists.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Roman fort found in Wales could prove myth of emperor’s camp is real

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Some of £2bn savings needed from energy budget expected to come from boiler upgrade scheme, sources say
Ministers are preparing to slash the amount of money available to subsidise heat pumps as they look for ways to fund higher defence spending, sources have told the Guardian.
Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, has been tasked with finding more than £2bn in savings from her budget to help pay for defence investment under a plan drawn up by the previous government.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ministers preparing to slash heat pump subsidies to fund defence spending

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
UK Health Security Agency notes above-average activity and urges at-risk groups to get vaccinated
Flu is striking earlier than usual in England, experts have said, insisting that vaccination is the best way to blunt its impact.
According to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), flu is at low levels, but various metrics, such as the proportion of positive tests and GP consultations for influenza-like illness, suggest it is on the rise, with the number of emergency-department attendances for influenza-like illness above seasonally expected levels.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flu cases higher than usual in England during September, experts say

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
As ‘one in, one out’ scheme ends, refugees still want to cross the Channel despite French police aggression and hostile welcomes
The smuggler works quickly. Using a small shovel, he digs up a dinghy buried in a sand dune on a beach not far from Boulogne-sur-Mer, assembles it and affixes a motor in record time.
“I never saw anyone work like this,” says Amad, from Iraq, one of a group of about 30 asylum seekers waiting to cross the Channel. “The UK government wants to stop the smugglers, but they are smart. They have plan A, plan B and plan C, so there is always a way for them to get people across this sea. For as long as asylum seekers will pay them, there is too much money involved for them to give up.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is there a different way to fix the small boats crisis?

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Although there is scepticism about Tehran’s capabilities, it has become clear it wants Britain to feel it poses a risk
Britain may have been only peripherally involved in the bombing of Iran that Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu started, but in the past fortnight it has become clear that Tehran wants to pose a threat inside the UK in response.
In the aftermath of the confused incident near RAF Fairford, western officials are weighing up whether to warn publicly that Iran now has US military targets in Europe on its mind, such as the air force base in Gloucestershire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: After RAF Fairford incident, how big a threat to the UK is Iran?

articles.author: Presented by Aditya Chakrabortty with Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor; produced by Frankie Tobi and Luke Smith; executive producers Maz Ebtehaj, Kirsty Major and James Tindale
articles.description:
Are we really living through ‘end-times fascism’? Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor think so.
In a new series from the Guardian, the pair speak to Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty in an extended interview. From Trump 2.0 and the rise of the tech billionaires to Gaza and the climate emergency, Klein and Taylor argue we are not just lurching from crisis to crisis but are in a new and dangerous moment in history. But they haven’t given up hope of a fightback
You can watch the full interview with Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor here.
Aditya’s suggested reading:
Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s End Times Fascism is out now and available here. It began life as a special essay in the Guardian, which you can read here.
A different take on whether Trump 2.0 is fascist comes from the economist Branko Milanović on his brilliant Substack.
Elon Musk gives Donald Trump millions, and Trump gives Musk vast access to power. To read more, look at Quinn Slobodian and Ben Tarnoff’s long read for the Guardian and their recent book Muskism: A Guide for the Perplexed.
For some phenomenal reporting on Trump’s second term, look at Regime Change by Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan.
How did the business class learn to love Trump and embrace chaos? Paul Heideman gives a lucid analysis in his recent book Rogue Elephant.
Klein and Taylor’s book regularly cites Karen Hao’s Empire of AI.
There’s also The Nerd Reich, just out from Gil Durán.
If you enjoyed Yanis Varoufakis in our last episode of Radical Thinking, check out his book Technofeudalism.
As for how AI is imposing a new age of total corporate control, The Rulers by Cecilia Rikap is a must.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Gaza is a moral tear in the universe’: Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor | Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty – podcast

articles.author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
articles.description:
Tories plan to scrap low-carbon housebuilding, Greens back new nuclear reactors, and Labour put oil-drilling decisions on hold
